meta.gift: speech, covenant, and the resonance that holds stone to stone
meta.waning: the Chord decays into echoes; oaths slip, bridges forget their arches
meta.curse_desc: the voices of the afflicted fade to a hum, and what they built beside begins to loosen
veils: The bells are not rung to honour the Chord but to drown out something singing underneath it.
The Chord is not fading — it is being sung backwards, deliberately, from somewhere beneath the oldest bell.
The backwards singer is the Chord's own first note, cast out so the harmony could begin; it does not want silence — it wants its place back.
meta.epigraph: Of the Founding Chord little now is spoken, and less is true. Gather what the old things still remember, and be sparing with belief.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the Founding Chord gave the world speech, covenant, and the resonance that holds stone to stone.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the Chord decays into echoes; oaths slip, bridges forget their arches.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the Founding Chord rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world speech, covenant, and the resonance that holds stone to stone.

e2.text: Ommoth, god of healing and the price of healing, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Nyorott, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Sylenmoth, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e5.text: Thaliast, god of secrets, locks, and the spaces between, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e7.text: The Bell of Ommoth was wrought as regalia of Ommoth's throne.

e9.text: The Hymn of Nyorott was wrought as regalia of Nyorott's throne.

e11.text: The Hymn of Sylenmoth was wrought as regalia of Sylenmoth's throne.

e13.text: The Chord of Thaliast was wrought as regalia of Thaliast's throne.

e14.text: Toressgrim, the Discordant, rose against the thrones. Thaliast led the gods to war.
e14.hidden: Sylenmoth treated with Toressgrim in secret and was spared what followed.

e15.text: Toressgrim was defeated and sealed beneath Ysiosreach; the seal was bought with the lives of 3 champions.

e16.text: The waning began: the Chord decays into echoes; oaths slip, bridges forget their arches. Mortals called the affliction the Unsinging: the voices of the afflicted fade to a hum, and what they built beside begins to loosen.

e17.text: Draansila Half-remembered founded the Order of the Chord at Loachgate, sworn to stand against the Unsinging.

e18.text: The Church of Ommoth was raised at Wrenwynreach; Nimaeast the Grey took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e19.text: Fendis the Twice-crowned was cast out of Church of Ommoth and founded the Cult of the Patient Below, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e19.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e20.text: Belawyn of the Last Door united the river-clans and was crowned in Mazucaelcrown; the realm took the name Ghalmundreach.

e21.text: At the urging of Nimaeast, the saint Sereth the Unbowed was given to the Founding Chord in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e21.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Nimaeast suspected as much.

e22.text: Thalulhild the Grey, sword-hand of Belawyn, opened the gates of Mazucaelcrown to the Order of the Chord over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e22.hidden: Thalulhild acted on a promise from the Cult of the Patient Below: that the marked of their house would be spared the Unsinging. The promise was not kept.

e23.text: Ghalmundreach fell. Belawyn of the Last Door died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e24.text: Thalulhild was found at Loachgate bearing the Unsinging, and was not spared.

e25.text: Sylenmoth, god of war and the keeping of thresholds, descended below the world to look upon the Founding Chord directly, and did not return.
e25.hidden: Sylenmoth found the truth of the waning, and chose to stay.

e26.text: Ulorast Last-sworn, last-sworn of the Order of the Chord, set out for the place where Sylenmoth was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e27.text: Word came that Ulorast fell to the marked, and then word came that Ulorast led the marked. The order believes neither.

e28.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the Patient Below were found digging at the seal of Toressgrim. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e28.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.

Thalulhild the Grey, sword-hand of Belawyn, opened the gates of Mazucaelcrown to the Order of the Chord over a grievance no chronicle agrees on. None now living can say whether Ghalmundreach fell. Belawyn of the Last Door died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again. The tellings differ, but most agree Thalulhild acted on a promise from the Cult of the Patient Below: that the marked of their house would be spared the Unsinging. The promise was not kept. Held long enough, it suggests the waning is no accident. The name endures; little else does.
